intended_object: The one-face polygon presentation of the normal-form nonorientable compact surface with p crosscaps and n boundary components. Its boundary word is a₁a₁…a_pa_p c₁h₁c₁⁻¹…c_nh_nc_n⁻¹. This is inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the comparison with `NonOrientableRel`.
explanation:
The body is `oneFacePresentation` applied to two things:
- the edge type `NonOrientableEdge p n`, with edges a_i, c_j and h_j;
- the word `nonOrientableBoundaryWord p n`. It concatenates the crosscap blocks [a_i, a_i] and then the boundary blocks [c_j, h_j, c_j⁻¹].

This is exactly the standard nonorientable normal-form word, as in Gallier–Xu Definition 6.5. It has length 2p + 3n, which the library proves. Each a_i and c_j occurs twice and each h_j once, so the h_j are the boundary contours. The word also matches the vendored `NonOrientableRel`, which glues the arcs of the closed disc in the same pattern (also of length 2p + 3n), and the library proves that the two realizations agree.

When p = 0, the word describes an orientable sphere with n holes. That case lies outside the admissible parameters and only follows the reference relation's convention, so it is not an error in the definition.

The construction is a specific combinatorial object in the library's own `SurfaceCellComplex` framework. Mathlib has no comparable notion of polygon presentations of surfaces, so the definition is not too narrow.
